content:
Following yesterday's system update that included security patches, Apple today released the security content details for Safari 26.6.1. The relevant information is as follows.

Codex appears multiple times in the CVE acknowledgements list

Apple today updated its "Apple Security Releases" page, which details the vulnerability fixes in Safari 26.6.1. This version is now available for macOS Sonoma and macOS Sequoia.

According to the document, this update contains 22 CVEs, all related to WebKit, including two vulnerabilities where "processing maliciously crafted web content could lead to memory corruption."

Notably, similar to recent security updates, OpenAI Codex Security appears nine times in the list, further highlighting the increasingly important role of AI tools in discovering vulnerabilities in Apple software.

Below is the full security content for Safari 26.6.1 released by Apple:

Safari 26.6.1 Released on August 18, 2026 WebKit Available for: macOS Sonoma and macOS Sequoia Impact: Processing maliciously crafted web content could lead to an unexpected Safari crash Description: An out-of-bounds access issue was addressed by improving bounds checking. WebKit Bugzilla: 317632 CVE-2026-64784: Janggoon Lee of Out of Bounds, OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett WebKit Description: The issue was addressed by improving memory handling. WebKit Bugzilla: 313452 CVE-2026-43795: wwwlk WebKit Bugzilla: 318348 CVE-2026-65338: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett WebKit Impact: Processing maliciously crafted web content could lead to memory corruption WebKit Bugzilla: 318405 CVE-2026-65341: Henock Habte WebKit Description: A memory corruption issue was addressed by improving locking. WebKit Bugzilla: 321480 CVE-2026-64782: Seonwook Kim, Shubham Chaskar, lattice, Josef Korbel WebKit Description: This issue was addressed by improving input validation. WebKit Bugzilla: 321484 CVE-2026-64781: Thomas Guillem WebKit Description: This issue was addressed by improving state management. WebKit Bugzilla: 321517 CVE-2026-65351: Niels Hofmans WebKit Bugzilla: 316996 CVE-2026-65340: Claudio Bozzato and Francesco Benvenuto of Cisco Talos, Josef Korbel (Citadelo) WebKit Bugzilla: 317142 CVE-2026-65337: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett WebKit Bugzilla: 317349 CVE-2026-65336: Josef Korbel WebKit Bugzilla: 316723 CVE-2026-65335: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett WebKit Bugzilla: 317603 CVE-2026-65333: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett WebKit Bugzilla: 317450 CVE-2026-65332: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett WebKit Bugzilla: 317611 CVE-2026-65331: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett WebKit Impact: Processing maliciously crafted web content could lead to an unexpected process crash Description: A use-after-free issue was addressed by improving memory management. WebKit Bugzilla: 316347 CVE-2026-64715: Hossein Lotfi (@hosselot) of TrendAI Zero Day Initiative WebKit Description: This issue was addressed by improving checks. WebKit Bugzilla: 316918 CVE-2026-64780: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett WebKit Description: A memory corruption issue was addressed by improving state management. WebKit Bugzilla: 316791 CVE-2026-65334: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett WebKit Description: A memory corruption issue was addressed by improving memory handling. WebKit Bugzilla: 317317 CVE-2026-43794: Dung Do (@_piers2) of Calif.io WebKit Impact: Processing maliciously crafted web content could lead to an unexpected process termination WebKit Bugzilla: 313703 CVE-2026-64787: 杉山 壮太, Shubham Chaskar WebKit History Impact: Visiting a maliciously crafted malicious website could lead to the disclosure of sensitive information WebKit Bugzilla: 315528 CVE-2026-64778: Mohit Negi WebKit Storage WebKit Bugzilla: 321485 CVE-2026-64779: Shubham Chaskar, Tommy DeVoss from Braze Security Team (@thedawgyg) Additional Acknowledgements WebKit We would like to acknowledge Henock Habte for their assistance.
